title: Americans Use Orange to Protest Gun Violence
main_content:
Mass shootings have become very common in the United States.

Some Americans want stronger gun controls. Others say people should be free to carry guns wherever they want to protect themselves.

Three years ago, a group of teenagers from the South Side of Chicago launched a campaign. The group asked their classmates to honor Hadiya Pendleton, a victim of gun violence, by wearing orange shirts.

The action has grown into a movement called Wear Orange. The hashtag #WearOrange can be seen all over Twitter and Facebook.

Many famous American buildings were lit up in orange on Thursday. One such building was the Empire State Building in New York City.

Many famous Americans and organizations expressed support for the movement.

Some people disagree that guns are the problem. One Twitter user wrote that “guns are not violent, people are.”

questions.question: Who did the teenagers from the South Side of Chicago want to honor?
Which famous building is mentioned in the text?
Do all people agree that guns are the problem?
options: Yes, everyone believes that guns are the issue
No, some believe that the problem lies with people

No, there is a division of opinion on the matter
questions.answer: No, there is a division of opinion on the matter
